Operator Czerny has demonstrated a remarkable aptitude for preservation of the front while inflicting Arts casualties on the enemy.

description.en: The moment an artist loses his untamed spirit, he has set foot upon the road to mediocrity. A musician who once stood at the zenith of his field, a genius who once used notes to challenge all the rules, has now draped himself in layers of chains. He has moved himself from Ewigegnade's concert halls to the children's piano room of some pharmaceutical company. The author hates to admit it, but it seems news of the death of legendary musician Czerny's talents is true. Was it to pander to the market? A yielding to reality? Or simply... the drying up of the wellspring of his talent? His recent creations are all, for the most part, mere echoes of his prior paradigms. It is clear he will be hard-pressed to create another piece as stunning as Morgen und Abend. A creative drought is truly a pity, but not something fellow musicians can criticize him too harshly for. —Journal of the Music Society of Leithanien Once more does Czerny stand at the heart of public opinion. Sharp, hypocritical voices. The critics reminisce about the brilliant Czerny who once stood under the spotlight. He may have been somewhat callous, but he interested them far more than the Czerny of today, who teaches piano to children and writes them textbook-style pieces to practice with. As for his naive students, they are aggrieved on his behalf. 'How could they say all that about you, Mr. Czerny?!' In the classroom, the red-faced child stops their performance, unable to stop themself from blurting out their feelings. Czerny does not raise his head, instead continuing to annotate his students' color-splashed score. 'Yes, yes, continue playing.' His voice is calm, yet it carries an unquestionable dignity. 'The arpeggios here are poorly shaped, these three bars are loose and feeble, and as for the tempo of this section... It's almost entirely wrong. Rather than worrying about meaningless noise, you had best focus on your fingers. Are you sure you practiced this week?' The child does not reply. He stops his annotating, looking up at the young face full of grievance, and he sighs. 'The truly useful assessments do not come from the mouths of others, but from here.' The stern teacher points at the metronome, then at the child's ears and chest. 'Do you hear it? This steady back-and-forth—tick, tock, tick, tock. It will not deviate, regardless of who you are, what talents you have, or what mood you are in. Fast is fast. Slow is slow. Wrong is wrong. 'It shall not fawn over you, nor kick you when you're down. 'It asks for absolute focus and consistent practice. 'It serves only music itself, so its assessment is a thousand times more honest than any person. 'Now, from the top!' ... It is late at night, long after the last child has left the piano room. Czerny sits before the piano, alone, with no complicated pieces in mind. He simply turns on the metronome, and to its mechanical tick-tock, meticulous newborn notes ring out from the black and white keys, bound to his heartbeat, bound to the pulse of the music.
description.zh:
不再桀骜不驯是艺术家走向平庸的开始。一位曾站在巅峰的音乐家，一位曾用音符挑战一切规则的天才，如今，正亲手为自己套上重重枷锁——从伊维格娜德音乐厅，到制药公司的儿童琴房。即便笔者不愿承认，但，传奇音乐家车尔尼的“艺术性死亡”，似乎已成事实。是向商业谄媚？向现实低头？还是……才华枯竭的标志？观其近期创作，大抵皆是对旧有范式的重复，显然，他已很难再拿出一首如《晨暮》般惊艳的曲子。江郎才尽，着实可惜，但各位同仁也不必过度苛责。
——《莱塔尼亚音乐学会会刊》
车尔尼又站在了舆论中心，这些声音尖锐、伪善。批评家们怀念那个聚光灯下锋芒毕露，甚至有些刻薄的车尔尼，现在这个每天给琴童上课、编写着一篇篇教课书式练习曲的车尔尼，让他们感到无趣。而他那些懵懂的学生，常为此愤愤不平。
“他们怎么能这样说您！”课堂上，憋红脸的孩子停下演奏，不禁嚷道。
车尔尼没有抬头，而是在被学生画得五颜六色的琴谱上留下了不少批注。“知道了，继续弹。”语调平静，却带着不容置疑的威严，“这里的琶音毫无章法，这三小节松散无力，这一大段的节奏……几乎全错。与其关注那些没营养的噪音，不如关注你的指尖——你这周真的有练琴？”
孩子不作声。
他顿了顿，看向那张稚嫩的、写满委屈的小脸，叹了口气。
“真正有用的评价，不在别人嘴里，在这儿。”严厉的老师点了点节拍器，又点了点孩子的耳朵、心口。
“听到了吗？这稳定的摆动声，滴，答，滴，答。它不会因你的身份、天赋或情绪而有丝毫的偏差，快就是快，慢就是慢，错就是错。
“它不会阿谀奉承，不会落井下石。
“它要求绝对的专注，持续的练习。
“它只服务于音乐本身，比任何人的评价都要诚实上万倍。
“现在，重来！”
……
已是深夜，最后一个孩子离开琴房。车尔尼独坐在钢琴前，没有演奏任何复杂的曲子。他只是打开了节拍器，就着机械重复的滴答声，在黑白琴键上落下崭新而严谨的音符，连通心跳，连通音乐的脉搏。
